review.summary: The phase-24 release-readiness chunk is strong, source-bound work. The recorded gate is a complete 73-command phase-24 run at the reviewed source hash a80368b6…, every check exit 0 with no timeouts and no unexecuted entries, and the resumable run records per-check source_unchanged plus checkpoint bindings for each generated receipt. Release readiness is genuinely extended to the selected version rather than reusing 0.2.2 helpers: scripts/check-access-release.py registers (24, '0.2.3'), demands schema-3 clean-package proofs from both compilers, binds the release commit to the current review fingerprint and ancestry, and byte-compares every packaged src/examples/README/LICENSE/NOTICE member against both the working tree and the release commit. The clean-package wrapper (scripts/check-management-package.py) requires actually executed cargo commands from an extracted archive plus four external example consumers and the frozen 3,820-probe consumer, and the retained receipts show 0.2.3 compiling and running on 1.89.0 and 1.99.0. Live evidence is honest and bounded: the schema-2 read-only receipt verifies only OAuth, records all four profiling_status probes as HTTP 403 permission prerequisites, and the ledgers correctly report liveVerified 1; tools/red_team_management.py:766 fails closed on a stale or non-read-only receipt. CHANGELOG.md documents the narrowed status domain, all five affected legacy values, profiling_status migration, the unchanged-wire caveat, the Unknown-to-named union transition, typed projection relocation, and the 403 outcome without implying acceptance. Rust evidence is substantive rather than nominal: tests/red_team_management_contracts.rs asserts exact per-page query pairs across list/pages/items/list_all, pre-auth rejection with zero token calls, five-operation sensitive response shapes in both modes, and credential redaction. The one real gap is documentation drift: docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md still presents the superseded 0.2.2 attempt-14 run (17 verified methods) as the current receipt while contracts/live-evidence.json now resolves to the 0.2.3 read-only receipt, and README/STABILITY direct consumers there as the live-acceptance authority. Two smaller items are an unreferenced failing receipt left in docs/checks and the live receipt not naming which endpoint profile the 403s came from.

findings.description: Stale live-acceptance narrative. Lines 13-22 state "The current 0.2.2 run is attempt 14", that it "verified 17 exact native methods from 24 service requests", and (line 35) that "the current receipt reference above identifies the applicable source and execution outcomes". The current reference contracts/live-evidence.json now resolves to docs/checks/phase-24-live-attempt-01.json, a schema-2 read-only receipt whose only verified workflow is oauth.get_token (liveVerified 1 in contracts/qualification.json:58 and contracts/native-operations.json). README.md:90-94 and docs/STABILITY.md:42 both direct consumers to this file as the authority for actual successful, blocked and unverified workflows, so the release candidate ships with documentation that overstates current live coverage. The file is also absent from the phase-24 and chunk scope_evidence lists, so no declared gate covers it.
findings.required_fix: Update docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md to describe the current 0.2.3 receipt (docs/checks/phase-24-live-attempt-01.json): one verified method (OAuth token exchange), four target-list filter probes rejected with HTTP 403 permission prerequisites, cleanupState not_needed, and the 0.2.2 attempt-14 results demoted to explicitly historical/archived. Add docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md to the phase-24 release-readiness chunk scope_evidence (new scope revision) so the gate covers it.

findings.description: An untracked receipt with "passed": false and "sourceUnchanged": false sits inside the phase-24 evidence directory under a directory named phase-24-routing-failure. Nothing in the repository references "routing-failure" (grep across the tree returns no matches), so there is no record of what produced it or why it failed. Because docs/checks/ is excluded from the review fingerprint, this artifact is invisible to the source hash yet visible to any later auditor reading the phase-24 evidence directory, where it can be mistaken for a failed phase receipt.
findings.required_fix: Either remove the orphan artifact, or retain it with an explicit explanation (e.g. a note in docs/CI.md or a sibling README) stating that it is a diagnostic capture of a concurrent private-material scan, is not phase evidence, and does not supersede docs/checks/phase-24-private-material.json.

findings.description: The read-only qualification exercised the api.sase.paloaltonetworks.com /ai-red-teaming/mgmt endpoint profile (crates/scm-sdk/examples/live_qualification.rs:56 and the allowlist at :268-283), not the SDK default DEFAULT_RED_TEAM_MGMT_ENDPOINT = https://api.apps.paloaltonetworks.com/ai-red-teaming/mgmt-plane (crates/scm-sdk/src/constants.rs:634-635). Neither READ_ONLY_LIMITATIONS (tools/live_evidence.py:102-106) nor CHANGELOG.md:56-62 names the endpoint profile actually probed, so a reader cannot tell which profile produced the four 403s. docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:192-195 requires qualifying selected profiles read-only and recording authorization/backend limitations per profile distinctly, and retaining current defaults unless evidence supports a reviewed migration.
findings.required_fix: Add an explicit limitation line naming the qualified endpoint profile (api.sase .../ai-red-teaming/mgmt) and stating that the SDK default api.apps .../ai-red-teaming/mgmt-plane profile was not exercised by this receipt, and mirror that sentence in the CHANGELOG 0.2.3 live-limitation bullet.

findings.description: Two readability/robustness nits in the new phase-24 branches. Line 60 uses a conditional expression as a statement (`publication.require_proof(proof, schema_version=3) if phase == 24 else publication.require_proof(proof)`), repeated at tools/release_delivery.py:197, discarding the value and obscuring control flow. Line 64 inserts str(root / "tools") into sys.path inside the per-compiler loop, so the entry is appended twice. Line 76 also compresses two different archive-location policies into one nested conditional expression that is hard to audit; for phase 24 it only requires the retained archive to live somewhere under .local/package-worktrees without binding it to the release commit's worktree (content is still bound via archive_sha256, files and validate_vcs against releaseCommit, so this is defense-in-depth only).
findings.required_fix: Replace the expression-statement conditionals with plain if/else statements, hoist the sys.path insertion out of the loop (or import once at module scope), and split line 76 into a named per-phase archive-location check that, for phase 24, requires the archive to resolve under .local/package-worktrees/<releaseCommit>/.

limitations: Read-only review: I executed nothing. All check outcomes are verified from the recorded receipts (exit codes, stdout/stderr, executed_at, source_unchanged, checkpoint_bindings) and from reading the verifier source that produced them. I did not recompute the source fingerprint, archive digests, or the checks-file SHA256, so I cannot independently distinguish a faithful receipt from one written by a trusted repository writer; docs/PHASES.md:7 states this trust boundary explicitly.

Generated model correctness was assessed from selected declarations in crates/scm-sdk/src/models/red_team_management.rs and crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs plus the recorded compiler and fixture evidence (14 check-rust receipts across both toolchains, generate_models --check and --verify-fixtures, two native-export receipts). I did not read the 180k-line generated file in full.

I did not open any credential or tenant-registration file, and I did not inspect .local/ contents beyond the paths named inside receipts. The retained package archives under .local/package-worktrees and .local/artifacts were therefore not hashed by me.

Live acceptance for the new profiling_status filter is unestablished by this evidence: all four probes returned HTTP 403. The receipt and the SDK documentation correctly record this as a permission prerequisite, but nothing here demonstrates that the filter is accepted or effective upstream, and the probes used the api.sase endpoint profile rather than the SDK default.

Publication, the remote annotated tag and terminal remote CI are out of scope for this chunk and remain unperformed; docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.3.json and release-tag-v0.2.3.json do not exist. The delivery chunk and final phase review must supply that evidence, and this readiness assessment cannot complete the phase (docs/PHASES.md:256-265).

The phase-24 evidence receipts (docs/checks/phase-24*.json, including both release-package proofs) were untracked at review time. That is consistent with the fingerprint exclusion of docs/checks/ in tools/review_phase.py:15, but it means I reviewed uncommitted evidence files; they must be retained in the evidence-only commit without retargeting the recorded release commit or archive digest.
